question: Should OpenClaw sponsor the RFC-backed Claw lifecycle and accept consented package content as managed agent-workspace files under this trust and ownership model?
rationale: Code review cannot decide whether this new persistent core lifecycle and package-content security boundary belong in the product; the PR also carries a protected maintainer label and depends on an unmerged stack.

options.title: Sponsor and land the stack
options.body: Approve the lifecycle and trust model, land the two base PRs first, and require exact-final-head proof for this slice.

options.title: Narrow the trust boundary
options.body: Keep the stack open while maintainers revise which workspace files packages may declare or how consent and ownership are represented.

options.title: Decline the lifecycle
options.body: Close the implementation stack if Claw-managed workspace mutation should not become an OpenClaw core capability.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and land the stack
recommendation.body: Approve the lifecycle and trust model, land the two base PRs first, and require exact-final-head proof for this slice.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository history ties this person most strongly to canonical shared-state and fs-safe infrastructure, and the unresolved choice is a core lifecycle product decision.
